data.description:
## Why
An agent that wants a new terminal already running a command has to create the surface and then `send`, and the send races shell startup. `new-workspace --command` does that race today and drops the queued result. Backlog item: C2.

## Evidence
- c11: `CLI/c11.swift:2213-2244` on origin/main (0ff8887e5e). `new-workspace --command` calls `workspace.create`, then `tab.send_text` with `unescapeSendText(commandText + "\\n")`, and discards the response (`:2241-2244`).
- c11: `new-split` (`:2247-2279`, method `tab.split`), `new-area` (`:2350-2377`, method `area.create`), and `new-tab` (`:2601-2623`, method `tab.create`) take cwd, title, and type. None takes `--command`. Help text at `:9010`, `:9137`, and `:9238` matches that.
- c11: `Sources/SocketHandlers/WorkspaceHandlers.swift:117-118` and `:232` pass `initial_command` into `addWorkspace` as `initialTerminalCommand`. That field replaces the shell. `Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift:3689-3709` writes it to `surfaceConfig.command` inside `withCString` before `ghostty_surface_new`.
- c11: `ghostty.h:447-450` already has both `command` (shell replacement) and `initial_input` (typed into the interactive shell). Nothing in Swift assigns `initial_input`.
- Upstream: cmux #9614 (`7a0ba63056`). The CLI sends `initial_input = text + "\r"` on split, pane create, surface create, and workspace create. Non-terminal types are rejected. Blank text is dropped. The shell outlives the command.
- Research: `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/06-grab-list.md` §1c. Fable row 4.3 (core). Astra row 4.3 raised the effort and marked it if-time. The backlog and `c11-1.0.html` revised decision keep it core.

## Scope
In: `--command` on `new-split`, `new-area`, and `new-tab`, carried as Ghostty `initial_input` with a trailing CR. Move `new-workspace --command` onto that same field. Reject it for browser and markdown. Drop blank text. Keep `initial_command` / `initialTerminalCommand` as the socket-only shell replacement.
Out: `launch-agent` prompt delivery (C11-258, and backlog C8). The bracketed-paste split (bug harvest #4). A delivery report that claims the command finished. `--command` together with `--layout` must not be invented as a second executor. Reject that pair with a clear error. The layout branch of `v2WorkspaceCreate` (`WorkspaceHandlers.swift:159-216`) returns before `initialTerminalCommand` is applied.

## Approach
Thread an `initial_input` string from the CLI through `tab.split`, `area.create`, `tab.create`, and `workspace.create`, and assign `surfaceConfig.initial_input` beside the existing `command` assignment, still inside a `withCString` that outlives `ghostty_surface_new`. Do not set `surfaceConfig.command` for this flag. Append `\r` in the app, not by reusing `unescapeSendText`, so a command that contains the two characters backslash-n stays literal. `new-workspace --command` stops calling `tab.send_text`. Return the created refs. Say in the human summary that the text was queued into the new shell, not that it ran. Update `skills/c11/references/api.md` and sync the installed c11 skill on the machine that lands the PR. Register feature flag `create.initial_input` if C6's list exists.

## Acceptance criteria
1. On a tagged build, `c11 new-tab --command 'printf hi-from-create'` shows `hi-from-create` in that tab, and the shell is still alive afterwards (`echo ok` works). The same for `new-split down` and `new-area`.
2. `c11 new-tab --type browser --command 'echo no'` and the markdown equivalent exit with a usage error and open nothing.
3. `c11 new-workspace --command 'printf ws-create'` no longer issues `tab.send_text`. The text appears in the new workspace's terminal, and a slow shell rc does not lose it the way a follow-up send can. Record one run where rc output arrives before the command echo, and say whether the command still ran.
4. `c11 new-workspace --layout <name> --command 'printf x'` fails with an error that names both flags. No workspace is left behind, or the error says a workspace was not created.
5. A socket `workspace.create` with `initial_command` still replaces the shell. A fixture or existing test covers that, so the two fields stay distinct.

## Validation
A `tests_v2` script against a tagged build's socket for the four create verbs, plus one computer-use check that the new terminal is readable and still at a prompt. No soak. Ghostty buffers `initial_input` in the PTY before rc files finish. The acceptance run in criterion 3 is the check that this is livable. Do not add a retry loop that sends the command again.

## Dependencies
None. Related to C3: once this lands, `new-workspace --command` no longer has a `queued` send result to surface. C3 documents send. This ticket documents create. Feature flag name lives with C6.

## Risks
Typing latency: this runs at surface create, not per keystroke. Do not add a display link or a manual draw. Main thread: surface creation is already on the spawn path. Do not block the socket worker on rc completion. Doctrine: the command is spawn config for c11's own terminal. No shell rc writes, no tenant config. Localization: new CLI errors go through `String(localized:)`. Six-locale fill is X1. Public repo: nothing sensitive.

Size: S. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: the shell stays the shell. `--command` types into it.
data.title: Type --command into a new terminal via Ghostty initial_input

data.body:
C11-280 review handoff at 812b26bd16d7a19dff13539bcb595512de2e2e18, branch c11-1.0/C11-280-initial-input. Integrated main base 43529df178a9cd8817fc092896efd2f3fcd63df5. Working tree clean; branch pushed. Evidence art_01M3XVTESJVCH2GNWE0N47QZ9M; exact-window capture art_01M3XVTEVZW7SY82KH6V0713XS.

All four create commands now queue literal command bytes plus one trailing CR (unless already present) in their single create RPC using Ghostty initial_input. Blank input remains absent. Browser/markdown/layout combinations reject before creation; CLI rejection precedes socket discovery. Flag-looking command bodies remain literal. initial_command and remote SSH startup remain distinct; successful native creation consumes input once and later reconstruction does not replay it. Responses report queued only. Typed create.initial_input capability enabled in CLI and server. New helper has app+CLI memberships, pure tests logic membership, native fixture host membership, all hand-added. Only the first main integration conflicted, in project.pbxproj: both additive membership sets retained; no resolution logic changes. Later main integrations were clean. No send/mailbox/SocketClient edits, Ghostty patch, tenant configuration writes, installed skill sync or owner self-review.

Observed validation:
1. Exact clean-head Atlas test invocation 71ad71fba4e4442594dc8f5e6d1430d4: compilation OK, actual test action OK, 10 CreateInitialInputTests + 2 CapabilityFeaturesTests + 1 CreateInitialInputRuntimeTests, zero failures. Native zsh rc delayed 2.106238 seconds: rc-start, rc-ready, initial, followup and reparent all PID 80876. Host-only native teardown/reattach created PID 81166 and a second slow rc; initial execution count remained exactly one and a new-shell followup succeeded. This is real Ghostty execution through existing runtime methods, not a product recovery UI claim.
2. Exact packaged Debug invocation 1e7e23b4a4d24191aec5c03ca08b3088: app executable SHA256 c51f45f649e90e4fe94e7c9a9f24069d3c728a24106b4d258eac86b3114b4944; bundled CLI SHA256 58294aa864acfb737e8b4f25c5ddf07986245f314ea7013a308c1447f7476362. Launched QA fresh on Atlas only, explicit /tmp/c11-debug-c11-280-input.sock. Executable fake-server fixture passed 126 positive creates and 18 rejection invocations: byte-exact escapes/Unicode/whitespace/CR, literal flags, JSON/human queued receipts, exactly one create, and rejected cases with zero connections. Fake replies prove CLI transport/rendering only.
3. Same packaged app: real new-workspace, new-tab, new-split and new-area queued-command outputs and surviving-shell followups passed. Unix proxy observed exactly one workspace.create carrying initial_input and no following tab.send_text. Capability advertised. Five CLI rejection shapes and 21 invalid RPC shapes preserved workspace/tab/area ID sets. Existing initial_command replaced the interactive shell: an explicit bounded shell program emitted its receipt and held a noninteractive process; a later shell command did not execute. All fixture workspaces closed. The explicit shell launcher accounts for Ghostty's Darwin exec-prefix behavior; product initial_command behavior was unchanged.
4. Exact tagged PID 49103, CGWindowID 7040, verified 1920x1080 Atlas display. Captured only that window and inspected the image: queued-command receipt and returned prompt are readable in a large single area, with THIS IS A DEV BUILD visible. Tree and screen oracle recorded alongside the screenshot. No Hyperion computer use or Tart guest.
5. Paired five-sample startup check against clean tagged main 43529df178, baseline invocation 34c5145fee584c99acf2bb2cbf611af2, same native submodule pins. Main median CLI return 1169.237 ms / observed receipt 1458.218 ms; candidate 899.745 / 1182.376 ms, all ten receipts observed. One-minute load differed (main 39.669, candidate 13.920); these are bounded smoke timings, not a causal speedup or soak-budget claim. Per-sample values and all load averages retained.

Atlas disk exhaustion interrupted one later gate; after the Orchestrator freed space, the final same-head build and all 13 tests succeeded. Superseded owned app copies pruned, logs/identities retained. Owned Atlas tag directories and apps are removed after evidence capture; no guest was created. GitHub CI and independent review are separate exact-head gates; neither is claimed green/complete here. Draft PR is opened only at handoff.

English keys for C11-291: cli.create.command.withLayout; cli.create.command.nonTerminal (one %@); cli.create.command.requiresValue; socket.create.initialInput.invalidType; socket.create.initialInput.unavailable. Machine marker input=queued has no unused localized label. Captain alone syncs installed skill sources after landing. Ghostty's input rail is used unchanged; the generic create-input rail could also benefit upstream.

Validator scenario:
1. Build merged main on Atlas with a unique tag, QA fresh, record artifact and CLI hashes. Run the four create commands with --command printing distinct assembled markers. Expected: each reply reports queued, each output marker appears exactly once, and follow-up echo works in the same shell. Observe create.initial_input in capabilities on the same artifact.
2. Trace new-workspace through an isolated Unix proxy. Expected: one workspace.create carrying literal bytes plus CR, no second send RPC. Exercise literal backslash-n, Unicode, leading/trailing whitespace, existing CR and flag-looking bodies; blank input omits initial_input.
3. Use the host native fixture with temporary HOME/ZDOTDIR and delayed rc, then reparent and reconstruct only its standalone surface. Expected: rc-ready precedes the one initial receipt; followup/reparent retain the original PID; reconstruction has a new PID and does not replay initial input. Record receipts separately from UI proof.
4. Reject nonblank browser/markdown creates, layout plus command, missing CLI value and non-string RPC input against listening/absent isolated sockets. Expected: precise errors, zero rejected CLI connections, no workspace/tab/area mutations. Verify an explicit bounded initial_command program remains a shell replacement rather than queued input.
5. Capture the exact tagged window by PID/window ID; inspect a readable terminal and returned prompt. Close all disposable workspaces, quit only the owned tagged apps, then remove owned Atlas tag directories and guests. Preserve production sessions, tenant files and installed skills.

Verdict: FAIL

Reviewed PR #522 at 812b26bd16d7a19dff13539bcb595512de2e2e18 against merge-base 43529df178a9cd8817fc092896efd2f3fcd63df5. Detached checkout was clean at intake and completion. One substantive static pass over all 16 changed files, their creation/launch/native-runtime seams, the ticket and plan, and the supplied Atlas evidence. No builds or tests run by this reviewer.

## Blocking

1. Public-board validation evidence contains prohibited local identity data. `.lattice/artifacts/payload/art_01M3XVTESJVCH2GNWE0N47QZ9M.json:114` and `:152` contain actual account-specific absolute home paths; `:306` contains the account-bearing shell prompt. The companion `.lattice/artifacts/payload/art_01M3XVTEVZW7SY82KH6V0713XS.png` visibly repeats that account name. Both are attached as validation evidence, and the JSON metadata marks the artifact `sensitive: false`. This violates reviewer-common's explicit public `.lattice` disclosure bar. These payloads are currently untracked in the main checkout, so this is an unsafe attached-evidence finding, not a claim that PR #522 has already committed or published them. Smallest fix: replace the attached evidence with sanitized public copies, using a neutral home-path placeholder and removing the identity-bearing prompt text/pixels while retaining the receipt, returned prompt, exact-head/build hashes and test outcomes. Ensure the original payloads are excluded from public board publication; merely attaching another copy leaves the originals reachable. No product-code redesign is needed.

## Non-blocking

None. No additional product-code defect found within the ticket's bounded scope.

The four ticket-owned CLI routes are new-workspace, new-tab, new-split and new-area. They carry literal input plus a trailing CR in the create RPC; new-workspace no longer sends a second RPC. CLI admission rejects the named nonterminal/layout combinations before connection, and server admission rejects them before creation. Both split outcomes, including fallback to a tab, pass the input through. Pointer lifetimes cover ghostty_surface_new; the pinned Ghostty implementation escapes then decodes its raw-input representation, preserving literal backslashes. Successful native creation clears the startup input; unsuccessful creation retains it. The enabled create.initial_input registry entry controls CLI/server admission. The new tests exercise executable behavior.

C11-258's agent.launch remains a distinct launch-plan/prompt-delivery path: its callers omit the new default-nil input argument and still use submitLaunchPlan after attention stamping. The ticket and plan expressly exclude moving launch-agent onto this feature.

## Runtime proof still required

The supplied exact-head Atlas artifact records 13 passing tests, including real delayed-rc execution, same-shell followup/reparenting, and reconstruction without replay. It also records the packaged four-create fixture, CLI request tracing, atomic CLI/RPC rejections, capability advertisement, and preserved initial_command shell-replacement behavior. I inspected the attached image: the receipt and returned prompt are readable. This is reviewed owner evidence, not an independent runtime rerun. Replace its unsafe public presentation as described above; no new behavior run is demanded solely for redaction.

At review time, PR head still matched the reviewed SHA. GitHub build, macOS compatibility and mailbox-unit checks were in progress; CI is not claimed green. Before landing, complete the required exact-head CI gates. If integration changes the reviewed source, run the ticket's bounded Atlas packaged-create/native-reconstruction proof against that integration head. No Hyperion runtime proof was performed or requested.

C11-280 round 1 disclosure repair at unchanged code head 812b26bd16d7a19dff13539bcb595512de2e2e18 (review ev_01M3XW9D57XKYNM5YJ12GPW0N4, finding 1).

Replacement evidence:
- JSON: art_01M3XWJ53T62F8V9WCQQBF37FR; SHA256 a7a303ef45a2250de1fe07742126499b5402eff8b16bddfe2f01dc24456aed02.
- PNG: art_01M3XWJ57BKY5EPX9SCWX1FQ9V; SHA256 82393937da2d580d62b2604d10931aa0a17c584d8f8c0a21f197ff782be770dc.

Home paths now use literal $HOME. Prompt account text is redacted in JSON and covered by two opaque rectangles in the screenshot. Decoded RGBA pixels outside those rectangles are byte-identical to the original; the receipt, returned prompt, readable area and DEV badge remain visible. Build identities, executable/CLI hashes, test receipts and outcomes are unchanged. The original screenshot hash remains as provenance; the screenshot_sha256 field identifies the sanitized PNG.

Deleted the two original untracked payload files for art_01M3XVTESJVCH2GNWE0N47QZ9M and art_01M3XVTEVZW7SY82KH6V0713XS; metadata is retained with missing payloads as requested. Two intermediate replacement payloads (art_01M3XWG2KZS30PEN3ZVRJNSRXP and art_01M3XWG2QKXWQ1HNYNB3672B1A) were also deleted after pixel verification caught a color conversion; only the final verified replacements above should be used. No code change, commit, push, rebuild or runtime rerun.

Validator scenario:
1. Open the replacement JSON. Expect literal $HOME for home paths, redacted prompt account text, unchanged head/build/CLI hashes, and all previously recorded test outcomes and receipts.
2. Open the replacement PNG. Expect opaque masks only over the account names, readable C11-280 execution receipt and returned interactive prompt, and the visible DEV badge.
3. Resolve both original metadata records. Expect metadata to remain and both original payload files to be absent.

Atlas cleanup verified: owned c11-280-input/baseline app processes, sockets and DerivedData directories are absent; owned tag directories c11-280-input, c11-280-baseline, c11-258-launch and c11-269-hygiene are absent. No Tart guests were created.

C11-280 scenario 3 host fixture fails on exact merged Batch 4 head 12d4f21a8822a3a7763d3a26b5295d8f6213c60a. Invocation 0cfce950cc1b4cf7ab249cd49b636d74: compile=ok, tests=failed, exit 65; six selected host tests ran, five passed and one failed. No overall C11-280 PASS recorded.

Actual failure after 3.378 seconds:

```text
CreateInitialInputRuntimeTests.swift:91:
XCTUnwrap failed: expected non-nil value of type UnsafeMutableRawPointer
native reconstruction must create another real PTY
```

The fixture had already created a real PTY, waited for its delayed rc, checked one initial-input receipt, executed a same-shell follow-up and reparented the same native surface. It then calls teardownSurface(), waits 100 ms, calls attachToView() on that same object and requires a new surface. There were no preceding assertion failures. The failure is not an observed startup/input replay or screen-lock allocation failure.

On this exact head, teardownSurface() seals portalLifecycleState as closed (Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift:3487). C11-295 commit f731745df1 deliberately added attachToView()'s live-state guard (line 3571), so the already-closed object cannot resurrect. The observed nil after teardown is consistent with that explicit lifecycle contract. The C11-280 fixture predates that merged guard. This source-grounded inference identifies a fixture-contract conflict; it is not a paired runtime regression classification.

Recommendation: retain the C11-295 no-resurrection contract and have the owner update the standalone reconstruction fixture to create a fresh valid object with consumed initial input omitted. Alternatively, accept the already-passed delayed-rc/one-receipt/same-PTY reparent portion and exclude the now-invalid resurrection assertion for this batch. The remaining C11-280 live/offline creation and visible terminal checks continue independently. No source/app/test edits, retries, or state-reset tricks were used to turn the result green.

The other selected host classes passed: StartupBundledReportsTests (one case) and TerminalControllerRefLifecycleTests (four cases). SocketStartupReadinessTests is a logic-target class and was exercised in the separate 2375-case logic gate, not counted as an executed host class. That logic gate passed with three existing skips and both approved class exclusions at this pre-C11-314 pin.

Recommend retaining C11-295 contract and owner fixture repair.

data.note: Orchestrator ruling: owner repairs fixture using fresh object; hold ticket open until fix-forward lands, then rerun only that fixture. Other scenarios continue.
